claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you check your eligibility for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking you about your child's age, as this is a key factor in determining eligibility.

**How old is your child?** 

Please let me know:
- Is your child **under 16 years old**, **between 16-19 years old**, or **20 years old or older**?

Also, I'll need to know the name of your child (or children if you have more than one) so I can track the assessment properly.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who is 17 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, **Alex, who is 17 years old**.

Since Alex is between 16-19 years old, I need to check whether Alex is in full-time education or training, as this affects eligibility.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to understand Alex's current educational status.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or training?**

Please let me know:
- **Yes** - Alex is currently in full-time education or training, OR
- **No** - Alex has left education/training recently (within the last 20 weeks), OR
- **Neither** - Alex is neither in education/training nor recently left

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in education or training at the moment. He left school a while back, more than 20 weeks ago.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. Since Alex left education more than 20 weeks ago and is not currently in education or training, let me navigate to check the eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that based on the eligibility rules, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's why:**

For a 16-19 year old to qualify for Child Benefit, they must be in approved full-time education or training. Since Alex left school more than 20 weeks ago and is not currently in education or training, he no longer qualifies as a "qualifying child" under the Child Benefit rules.

**Important Information:**

The guidance does note that if a 16-17 year old leaves education, Child Benefit can continue for up to **20 weeks** if they register with:
- The careers service, or
- The armed services

Since Alex has been out of education for more than 20 weeks, this extension period has passed.

**What you can do:**

If Alex's circumstances change and he enters approved full-time education or training before turning 20, you could potentially reapply. Otherwise, Child Benefit eligibility will cease for Alex until his situation changes.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. That's disappointing, but I understand. Just to be clear though - Alex actually works full-time now at a local shop. Does that make any difference to the eligibility?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: That's a good question! Let me check the rules more carefully. The fact that Alex is working full-time is actually relevant to the eligibility criteria. Let me navigate back to check the specific rules about full-time work.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Ah, I see now - this is an important clarification! Thank you for mentioning that Alex works full-time.

**Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week** at the local shop? Or is it less than 24 hours per week?

This is actually a key factor in the eligibility assessment. If Alex is working 24 hours or more per week and is not in approved education or training, this would affect the eligibility determination.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he works full-time - definitely more than 24 hours a week at the shop.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. Since Alex is working 24 hours or more per week and is not in approved education or training, this means he is not a qualifying child for Child Benefit purposes.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm afraid the outcome remains the same: **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's the specific reason:**

Since Alex is aged 16 or over, is working 24 or more hours per week at the shop, and is not in approved education or training, he does not qualify as a "qualifying child" under the Child Benefit rules.

**Key Guidance:**

Child Benefit stops when a child aged 16 or over starts paid work for 24+ hours per week and is no longer in approved education or training. 

**If circumstances change:**

If Alex were to return to approved full-time education or training, you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. However, while he continues in full-time work (24+ hours per week) without also being in approved education/training, he cannot be claimed for.

I understand this is disappointing news. Is there anything else I can help clarify about the eligibility rules?

Now let me provide you with the final eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Final Eligibility Decision:**

**Child Name:** Alex  
**Age:** 17 years old  
**Eligibility Status:** ❌ **NOT ELIGIBLE**

**Summary:**
You are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex because he is working full-time (more than 24 hours per week) and is not in approved full-time education or training. The eligibility rules require that 16-19 year olds must be in approved education or training to qualify.

If you have any other questions or if Alex's situation changes in the future, feel free to reach out!
